description: Optional inspiration palette of clinical-reasoning strategies. NOT consulted by runtime routing — the primary agent picks strategies ad-hoc or selectively opens this file. Full-catalog loading is a contract violation (#205 AC7).

strategies.name: Likelihood-ratio thinking
strategies.description: Reason about test results as multipliers of pre-test odds — LR+ of 10 multiplies the odds by 10; LR− of 0.1 divides by 10. The intuition transfer is: pre-test probability is load-bearing for how informative a result is.

strategies.name: Rule-out vs rule-in tests
strategies.description: Sensitive tests are for ruling out (a negative is informative); specific tests are for ruling in (a positive is informative). Strong teaching point for cases where a sensitive-but-not-specific test is over-trusted as a confirmatory result.

strategies.name: Test cost vs information gain
strategies.description: What is the cheapest test that produces the largest probability update? Cost includes financial, time, patient burden, and downstream-cascade considerations. Red-flag-advocate's ruling-out test draws on this strategy.

strategies.name: Anchoring-bias defense
strategies.description: Explicit cognitive-bias defense: what if the first plausible diagnosis is wrong? What would the clinician miss by anchoring? Pairs naturally with mnemonic-driven enumeration and must-not-miss-first structures.

strategies.name: Absolute vs relative risk framing
strategies.description: Reason about treatment-effect literature in both absolute and relative terms. NNT (number-needed-to-treat) translates relative-risk reductions into individual-patient-scale numbers. Strong fit for cases whose teaching point is interpreting RCT effect sizes.

strategies.name: Frequentist vs Bayesian framing
strategies.description: Contrast a p-value (frequentist) with a posterior probability (Bayesian). When the literature reports p-values, the Bayesian translation requires explicit pre-test priors. Strong fit for evidence-tier-walking paths.
